The Supervising Officer on duty at Reception when Mr Talbot arrived had never received training in her duties but merely gained experience by shadowing another officer. It did not appear that any written material was provided so as to inform her of her duties, including the PSI
lack of written training material for reception staff

A Senior Officer gave mouth to mouth resuscitation to Mr Talbot without the use of a guard. It is understood that although mandatory for more junior officers at HMP Preston, carrying a breathing guard at all times is discretionary for certain senior grades.
absence of breathing guard during resuscitation

It is understood that following the death of a prisoner a notice to this effect is issued to the prisoners and staff but that staff are not informed of the manner of an unnatural death. Thus, it appeared that staff attending to give evidence at the inquest were unaware of another recent previous death involving a plastic bag
lack of awareness of prior death involving plastic bag

The evidence disclosed the need for healthcare and the prison to devise a better means of communication between healthcare personnel at the scene of a medical emergency and the prison control room / ambulance control
lack of communication between healthcare personnel and ambulance control

Similar communication difficulties have already been reported in relation to the inquest into the death of Martin Brown who died at HMP Lancaster Farms and the Prison and Probation Ombudsman has highlighted a delay in the provision of essential 1 information to Ambulance Control in the case of at HMP Garth who died on 9th December 2020
delayed provision of essential information to ambulance control
The fact that communication difficulties have arisen between healthcare and the ambulance service in three recent cases involving prisons in Lancashire may indicate a potentially national problem
potential national communication failure between healthcare and ambulance service
